description: Bug-class taxonomy. observation_signals match black-box evidence; source_signals match code. evidence_level is verified only when a chain card in knowledge/chains/ proves the class was solved here.

evidence_levels.verified: at least one verified chain card names this class; verified_by lists them
evidence_levels.catalogue: standard published class, no local solve yet; the skill is a starting point, not proven local knowledge

rules: A signal match is a candidate, never proof. Run the class's first_probe.
A class whose falsifier is observed is closed for this challenge, with the observation recorded.
evidence_level is raised to verified only by tools/classify_solve.py after a flag is verified.
confusable_with names classes that share signals; check those before committing to one.

classes.name: SQL injection
observation_signals: syntax error|sqlstate|you have an error in your sql
classes.first_probe: one syntax marker, then a matched true/false pair against the same input
classes.falsifier: for an immediate sink, identical validated response for the true and false forms; for a stored or deferred sink, the same result after the consumer is triggered

classes.name: NoSQL / operator injection
classes.first_probe: send the filter pinned to an object you created, with every write field omitted, and read what comes back
classes.falsifier: the value is coerced to a string, so no object reaches the query
classes.blast_radius: a broad filter combined with write fields rewrites the whole collection

classes.name: OS command injection
classes.first_probe: one benign separator with a command whose output is unmistakable, and a timing variant as a fallback channel
classes.falsifier: the value is passed as a single argv element, never through a shell

classes.name: Server-side template injection
classes.first_probe: one arithmetic marker; confirm the engine from the evaluated form or the error string before any chain
classes.falsifier: the marker is reflected literally, which is an XSS shape rather than template evaluation

classes.name: XML external entity
classes.first_probe: one entity pointing at a path the target certainly has, and an out-of-band entity when nothing is echoed
classes.falsifier: the parser is configured with entity resolution disabled

classes.name: Server-side request forgery
classes.first_probe: one address you control, then the same request against an internal-only address, comparing status and timing
classes.falsifier: the fetch target is fixed in source and the request never influences it

classes.name: Request smuggling / CRLF injection
classes.first_probe: one folded control character inside the interpolated value; compare the upstream error with an ordinary hostname
classes.falsifier: the value is percent-encoded or validated, so no control character survives into the outbound request
classes.blast_radius: a smuggled request executes against the backend as a trusted client; it can change state for everyone

classes.name: Parser differential / proxy trust
observation_signals: inspects the raw body|raw body before a decoder|before a decoder runs
classes.first_probe: send the same authenticated-only request twice, once normally and once with the proxy header named in the Connection header
classes.falsifier: both forms are rejected, so the trust check does not depend on that header

classes.name: Cross-site scripting
classes.first_probe: one unique harmless marker; find which context it lands in before choosing any payload
classes.falsifier: nothing renders the injected markup, so there is no viewer and no flag path

classes.name: Cross-site request forgery
classes.first_probe: a cross-origin form whose content type the endpoint still accepts, submitted by the viewer you control
classes.falsifier: the endpoint requires a token the attacker page cannot read or a content type a form cannot produce

classes.name: CORS misconfiguration
classes.first_probe: repeat an authenticated request with a foreign Origin and read whether the origin is reflected alongside credentials
classes.falsifier: the allowed origin is a fixed allowlist, or credentials are not permitted

classes.name: Open redirect
classes.first_probe: one external destination in the redirect parameter, following the response Location header exactly
classes.falsifier: the destination is validated against an allowlist or forced to a relative path

classes.name: Cache poisoning / deception
classes.first_probe: send an unkeyed header with a unique marker, then request the same URL cleanly and look for the marker
classes.falsifier: the header is part of the cache key, so the poisoned copy is never served to anyone else
classes.blast_radius: a poisoned entry is served to every other player until it expires

classes.name: Prototype / class pollution
classes.first_probe: pollute one harmless property, then read it back through a path that should not have it
classes.falsifier: the merge rejects reserved keys, or nothing reads the polluted property with a fallback
classes.blast_radius: pollution is global to the process: every later request inherits it until restart

classes.name: Unsafe deserialization
classes.first_probe: identify the format from the blob's own magic before touching any gadget
classes.falsifier: the blob is signed with a key that is not leaked and not reachable

classes.name: Race condition / TOCTOU
classes.first_probe: two interleaved requests, not a flood: the point is to land the second commit inside the window, and a flood hides which one did
classes.falsifier: the read and the write happen inside one transaction or behind one lock
classes.blast_radius: racing a shared resource can corrupt it for other players; race an object you own

classes.name: Business logic / mass assignment
classes.first_probe: one extra field the model has but the form does not send, or one step of the flow skipped
classes.falsifier: the handler reads an explicit allowlist of fields and ignores everything else

classes.name: Authentication and session
observation_signals: (?:signature|\bmacs?\b|hmac|hash|integrity check)[^\n]{0,45}(?:does not cover|only covers?|covers? only|computed over only|applied to a prefix|prefix of)
classes.first_probe: decode and read the token before modifying anything; the weakness is usually visible in the header or the claims
classes.falsifier: the signature is verified with a key that is neither leaked nor guessable

classes.name: OAuth / SSO flow
classes.first_probe: walk the whole flow once and record every redirect, parameter and cookie set, before changing any of them
classes.falsifier: the state parameter is bound to the session and the redirect target is a strict allowlist

classes.name: Broken object-level authorization
classes.first_probe: create an object as one identity, then request its identifier as a second identity
classes.falsifier: the handler scopes the lookup by the authenticated owner

classes.name: Arbitrary file read / source disclosure
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:file\ read\ primitives|arbitrary\ file\ read|source\ disclosure|read\ primitives|read\-primitives)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: an absolute path to a file the target certainly has, before trying any traversal
classes.falsifier: the path is resolved and confined to a fixed directory

classes.name: Unrestricted file upload
classes.first_probe: a benign marker file first; the question is where it is stored and what later reads or executes it
classes.falsifier: the stored file is renamed, served with a fixed type, and never parsed again

classes.name: GraphQL abuse
classes.first_probe: one introspection query; if it is disabled, one field-suggestion error to recover names
classes.falsifier: introspection is off and errors reveal no field names

classes.name: Smart contract / web3
classes.first_probe: read the setup contract and the solved condition first; that names the exact state you must reach
classes.falsifier: the solved condition depends on state no external caller can change

classes.name: Cross-site leak / browser side channel
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:browser\ side\ channel|cross\-site\ leak|web\ xs\ leaks|xs\ leaks|xs\-leaks)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: decide first where attacker code may run: if CSP or a URL allowlist keeps you from executing script on any origin the bot can reach, enumerate every piece of server state a plain GET from the bot can change, and use that as the read-back channel
classes.falsifier: the bot can reach no attacker-influenced state at all, and no observable on the target changes as a function of what the victim's browser loaded
classes.blast_radius: the read-back channel is often a shared cache or store; filling it to force eviction destroys every other key, so never run it against an instance someone else is using

classes.name: Authentication and logon trace
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:authentication\ and\ logon\ trace|dfir\ authentication\ trace|authentication\ trace|authentication\-trace)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: filter the event set to 4624 and read the LogonType and IpAddress fields of the first match
classes.falsifier: no authentication record names a source address or an account outside the host's own service accounts, and every logon is type 5 service or type 0 system

classes.name: Process execution trace
classes.first_probe: filter to Sysmon event 1 or Security 4688 and read the CommandLine and ParentImage of the first match
classes.falsifier: no event 1, 4688, 4103 or 4104 exists in the set, and every process artifact present names a signed binary under the system directory with no command line carrying a URL or an encoded run

classes.name: Host persistence trace
classes.first_probe: read the Run and RunOnce values and the Services subkeys from the SOFTWARE and SYSTEM hives, and compare each image path against the intrusion window
classes.falsifier: every autostart entry and service image path resolves to a signed vendor binary whose file creation time predates the intrusion window

classes.name: Filesystem metadata timeline
classes.first_probe: build a bodyfile from the filesystem metadata and read the entries inside the intrusion window in chronological order
classes.falsifier: no file was created, renamed or deleted inside the intrusion window outside routine operating-system paths, and the $STANDARD_INFORMATION and $FILE_NAME timestamps agree on every candidate

classes.name: Network and exfiltration trace
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:network\ and\ exfiltration\ trace|dfir\ network\ exfil\ trace|network\ exfil\ trace|network\-exfil\-trace)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: read the per-peer byte counts in each direction and identify the peer with the largest outbound volume, then join it to the owning process
classes.falsifier: every outbound conversation resolves to a vendor update or telemetry endpoint, and the largest outbound volume in the window is smaller than a routine update

classes.name: Cloud audit trail
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:dfir\ cloud\ audit\ trace|cloud\ audit\ trace|cloud\ audit\ trail|cloud\-audit\-trace)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: extract eventTime, eventName, sourceIPAddress and userIdentity.arn from every record, sort by time, and read the first action that is not a read
classes.falsifier: every recorded action belongs to a service principal or an automation role whose behaviour is unchanged across the whole window, and no credential or policy object was created or modified

classes.name: Anti-forensics and log tampering trace
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:anti\-forensics\ and\ log\ tampering\ trace|dfir\ antiforensics\ trace|antiforensics\ trace|antiforensics\-trace)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: look for Security 1102 and, whether or not it is present, read the event record identifiers in order and report the largest discontinuity
classes.falsifier: record identifiers are contiguous across the whole window, no 1102 or 104 exists, and the $STANDARD_INFORMATION and $FILE_NAME timestamps agree on every file created in the window

classes.name: RSA key or plaintext recovery
classes.first_probe: answer the six discriminators in order with python3 tools/crypto_attack.py list, then run the ONE attack they select: how many moduli, is e small, is d small, are the primes close, is part of a factor known, is phi shared
classes.falsifier: the attack's own stated applicability bound is exceeded -- for example d above the 0.292 bound for boneh-durfee, or a known-bits window above n**0.25 for coppersmith -- and no lattice parameter moves it

classes.name: Predictable pseudorandom generator
classes.first_probe: name the generator from source, count how many consecutive outputs you hold, then run the matching attack id (lcg-recover, lcg-unknown-modulus, lcg-truncated, berlekamp-massey, lfsr-recover, lfsr-predict, mt19937-clone)
classes.falsifier: predict one held-back output and compare: a generator whose next value you cannot produce exactly is not recovered, and mt19937-clone genuinely needs 624 consecutive 32-bit outputs

classes.name: Curve, nonce or discrete-log recovery
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:curve,\ nonce\ or\ discrete\-log\ recovery|crypto\ ecc\ dlog|ecc\ dlog|ecc\-dlog)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: decide the discriminator first: a nonce REUSED across two signatures recovers the key in closed form with ecdsa-nonce-reuse and needs no lattice, a merely BIASED nonce is hnp or hnp-ecdsa, and a plain discrete log needs the smoothness check before bsgs or pohlig-hellman
classes.falsifier: re-derive the public point from the recovered private scalar and compare: a scalar that does not reproduce the supplied public key is not the key, and bsgs is out of reach above a group order of roughly 2**44

classes.name: Block, stream or MAC oracle
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:block,\ stream\ or\ mac\ oracle|crypto\ symmetric\ oracle|symmetric\ oracle|symmetric\-oracle)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: detect ECB in ONE request wherever you control plaintext -- identical plaintext blocks give identical ciphertext blocks -- then separate an invalid-pad answer from an invalid-MAC answer before writing any oracle loop
classes.falsifier: the mode is authenticated (GCM or an HMAC checked before decryption), so a tampered ciphertext is rejected identically whatever the padding, and no oracle exists to query

classes.name: Stack memory corruption
classes.first_probe: run python3 tools/pwn_triage.py on the binary FIRST for the protections with the evidence that decided each, then measure the exact offset to the saved return address empirically with a pattern you generate yourself -- pwntools is absent here
classes.falsifier: the read is bounded by a length the input cannot influence, so no write reaches saved state; note that a STATIC binary carries __stack_chk_fail even when built -fno-stack-protector, so confirm a canary from the %fs:0x28 load in the disassembly rather than from the import

classes.name: Format-string read or write
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:format\-string\ read\ or\ write|pwn\ format\ string|format\ string|format\-string)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: send a handful of %p in one request and read the leaked words back, which is the cheapest confirmation in pwn, then locate your own buffer with %N$p before deciding read against write
classes.falsifier: the format argument is a literal and the user value is an argument to it, so nothing is interpreted; and full RELRO reported by tools/pwn_triage.py closes the GOT-overwrite route whatever the leak is worth

classes.name: Heap allocator corruption
classes.first_probe: answer the glibc version question first, because tcache behaviour, double-free detection and fd mangling differ sharply across versions, then map the allocation lifecycle and name the primitive the bug gives before choosing any technique
classes.falsifier: the pointer is cleared on free and every index is bounds-checked, so no freed object is reachable; gdb is absent here, so runtime confirmation is radare2 in debug mode or observable program behaviour

classes.name: ROP and code reuse
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:rop\ and\ code\ reuse|pwn\ code\ reuse|code\ reuse|code\-reuse)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: this class presupposes control of the instruction pointer, so confirm that first; then read the protections to decide whether a leak is needed at all, and build the leak chain and verify the leaked value looks like a libc address before chaining further
classes.falsifier: the gadgets present cannot express the call -- no controllable argument register, or no writable page to pivot into -- which tools/pwn_triage.py reports from the executable segments it actually scanned, since ROPgadget and ropper are absent here

classes.name: Native deciding check
classes.first_probe: locate the input read, follow the value to the comparison, and quote the disassembly that carries it: a described check is not a measured one. r2 -A then afl then pdf @ main; gdb is absent, so r2 -d is the debugger
classes.falsifier: the comparison is against a value computed at run time from something you cannot observe or supply, so replicating the check in python cannot produce the input

classes.name: Managed runtime decompilation
classes.first_probe: confirm the runtime from the header and quote the bytes -- a PE with a non-zero CLR data directory, or the 0xCAFEBABE magic -- then decompile with what exists here: ilspycmd for .NET, javap plus unzip for Java. jadx, procyon and mono are absent
classes.falsifier: the assembly is a thin native stub and the logic is in an unmanaged module, so no managed decompiler reaches it and the work belongs to rev-native-check

classes.name: Script bytecode or custom VM
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:script\ bytecode\ or\ custom\ vm|rev\ bytecode\ vm|bytecode\ vm|bytecode\-vm)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: for a .pyc read the header magic and name the python version before running any decompiler, falling back to the stdlib dis module on the unmarshalled code object when uncompyle6 refuses; for a custom VM recover the OPCODE TABLE before reading one instruction of its program
classes.falsifier: the dispatch loop is data-driven from a table that is itself generated at run time, so a static table recovery is incomplete and the program must be traced instead

classes.name: Media and document metadata
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:media\ and\ document\ metadata|osint\ media\ metadata|media\ metadata|media\-metadata)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: run exiftool and read ALL of its output rather than grepping one tag, then binwalk and strings for appended or embedded data; steghide, zsteg and outguess are absent here, so never claim an extraction with them
classes.falsifier: the metadata was stripped on upload and the carrier holds no appended data, so the answer is only in the visible frame and becomes a hypothesis rather than a measurement

classes.name: Identity and handle pivot
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:identity\ and\ handle\ pivot|osint\ identity\ pivot|identity\ pivot|identity\-pivot)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: extract the single most UNIQUE pivot and normalise it -- compute the key fingerprint rather than eyeballing it -- then produce an ordered plan of at most six queries, each with its source and the one fact it would confirm, for ctf-writeup-scout to run
classes.falsifier: the pivot is too generic to separate from unrelated accounts, which is a measurement about the pivot and means a different one must be extracted rather than the same one searched harder

classes.name: Domain, DNS and certificate records
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:domain,\ dns\ and\ certificate\ records|osint\ infra\ records|infra\ records|infra\-records)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: query TXT first because that is where a flag is actually planted, then sweep the record types that can carry data, then whois, then the certificate and its subject alternative names, which routinely leak the sibling hostname that is the real next step
classes.falsifier: every record type returns only operational data and the certificate names no host the challenge did not already supply, so the answer is not in the live records and only an archived or transparency source could carry it

classes.name: Restricted interpreter escape
classes.first_probe: MAP THE FILTER before writing an escape: send single probe characters and short tokens until the blocked bytes, names and node types are known and the layer the check runs at is named, because that mapping is the challenge and the escape is mechanical afterwards
classes.falsifier: the check runs on the parsed AST and rejects every node type that can reach an attribute or a call, so no expression in the remaining grammar reaches a live object

classes.name: Encoding or carrier puzzle
observation_signals: (?<![a-z0-9])(?:encoding\ or\ carrier\ puzzle|misc\ encoding\ carrier|encoding\ carrier|encoding\-carrier)(?![a-z0-9])
classes.first_probe: IDENTIFY THE CARRIER before decoding: the alphabet, the distinct-character count and the length modulus separate base64 from base32 from base85 from hex from a custom alphabet in one command, and the index of coincidence separates a substitution from a transposition from a Vigenere
classes.falsifier: the alphabet and length match no standard carrier and the index of coincidence is outside the natural-language range, so it is neither a standard encoding nor a classical cipher and the structure of the container is the real hiding place
